This manual is for the Hearthline T2 thermostat with firmware 1.4. Firmware is the software inside the device. This product is a smart thermostat for homes that have a gas or oil boiler. A boiler heats water for home heating and/or hot water.

# Safety Information

- A qualified installer must install the receiver box. The receiver box is the small unit wired next to the boiler. This manual covers setup after the installer has finished that work.
- A qualified installer must do any work on a gas or oil boiler. Do not move, connect, or change boiler wiring yourself.
- The receiver box must only be opened by a qualified installer. It is mains powered. Mains power means the house electricity supply.
- Do not install the wall unit in direct sunlight or above a radiator. Strong heat and direct sun can make the wall unit read the room temperature poorly. They can also make the touch screen harder to use.
- Keep the wall unit and receiver box dry. Do not install them where they may be splashed by water. Do not touch them with wet hands.
- Keep AA batteries, loose wiring, and small parts away from children. If the wall unit is wired with 24 V AC, a qualified installer must connect that wiring. AC means alternating current, a type of low-voltage electrical power.

# Getting Started

## How to

This section helps you pair the wall unit with the receiver box, connect to Wi-Fi, and create an app account.

1. Check that a qualified installer has finished installing the receiver box next to the boiler. The receiver box receives radio messages from the wall unit and controls the boiler.
2. Keep the wall unit within the radio range of the receiver box. The receiver and wall unit can talk to each other by radio at up to 30 m indoors.
3. If your wall unit uses batteries, put in two AA batteries. The wall unit runs on two AA batteries. The battery life is about 2 years. Battery life can vary with use.
4. If your wall unit uses wiring, it runs on 24 V AC wiring. A qualified installer must do this wiring. Do not connect wiring yourself.
5. Turn on the wall unit. If the screen does not turn on, check the batteries or ask your installer to check the 24 V AC wiring.
6. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Getting Started > Pairing**. Follow the prompts on the screen.
7. Wait while the wall unit looks for the receiver box. Keep the wall unit and receiver box close for the first pairing. This can help the radio link connect more easily.
8. Confirm the wall unit and receiver box are paired. The wall unit should show that it is connected to the receiver box.
9. Connect the wall unit or receiver box to your home internet. Go to **Menu > Getting Started > Wi-Fi**. Wi-Fi is wireless internet.
10. Choose your home Wi-Fi network. The T2 uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only. Do not try to use a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network.
11. Enter your Wi-Fi password carefully. Wi-Fi passwords can contain capital letters, small letters, numbers, and symbols. A wrong password will stop the connection.
12. Wait until the wall unit or app shows that the device is online. If it does not, check that your phone is on the same 2.4 GHz network and that the password is correct.
13. Download the Hearthline app on iOS or Android. The app is available for iOS and Android phones and tablets.
14. Open the Hearthline app and create an account. You will need an email address and a password. Use a password you can remember.
15. Add your home and thermostat to the app. Follow the app prompts until the T2 appears in your list of devices.
16. Set your language, temperature unit, and time format. Go to **Menu > Settings > Language** to choose English, French, German, or Spanish. Go to **Menu > Settings > Temperature Unit** to choose °C or °F. Go to **Menu > Settings > Time Format** to choose 12 h or 24 h.
17. Try a simple setting. Open the wall unit menu and choose **Menu > Heating > Manual**. Change the target temperature slightly. Check that the wall unit responds.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Language | English, French, German, Spanish | English |
| Temperature unit | °C or °F | °C |
| Time format | 12 h or 24 h | 24 h |

## Troubleshooting

- If pairing fails, check that the wall unit is within 30 m indoors of the receiver box. Move the wall unit closer, then go to **Menu > Getting Started > Pairing** again.
- If the wall unit does not turn on, check that two AA batteries are installed correctly. If the wall unit uses 24 V AC wiring, ask a qualified installer to check the wiring.
- If Wi-Fi will not connect, check that you are using a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network. The T2 does not use 5 GHz. Check the Wi-Fi password and try again from **Menu > Getting Started > Wi-Fi**.
- If the app cannot find the device, check that the wall unit is online. Also check that your phone has a working internet connection.
- If the wall unit language is wrong, go to **Menu > Settings > Language** and choose English, French, German, or Spanish.
- If times look wrong, go to **Menu > Settings > Time Format** and choose 12 h or 24 h. Make sure the time format matches how you want to read times.
- If the receiver box is not responding, do not open it. Check that it has mains power. If the problem continues, contact a qualified installer.

# Manual Temperature Control

## How to

Manual temperature control lets you change the temperature without changing your weekly schedule. The wall unit has a 3.5-inch touch screen and a rotating ring. The rotating ring is a round control you can turn to change values.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Manual**. The screen shows the current target temperature.
2. Turn the ring or use the touch screen to raise or lower the target temperature. You can choose 5 °C to 30 °C in 0.5 °C steps. The default target temperature is 20 °C.
3. Confirm the target temperature. The wall unit will use this temperature as long as your hold setting allows it.
4. If you only want the change for a short time, set a hold duration. Go to **Menu > Heating > Manual > Hold Duration**.
5. Choose **Until next schedule change** if you want heating to return to the normal schedule at the next time your schedule changes. This is the default.
6. Choose a fixed hold if you want the new temperature for 1 to 12 hours. Use the ring or touch screen to choose the number of hours.
7. Choose **Permanent** if you want the manual temperature to stay until you change it again. Use this with care. A permanent hold can stop your normal schedule.
8. In the Hearthline app, open your home and go to **Menu > Heating > Manual**. You can set the same target temperature and hold duration there.
9. When a hold ends, the wall unit follows your normal schedule again if a schedule is active. If there is no schedule, it keeps using the last manual setting.
10. If your home uses a gas or oil boiler, changing the target temperature tells the thermostat when to ask the boiler to heat. The actual heat change may take some time.
11. If you set a target close to the current room temperature, the boiler may not run. This is normal. The boiler runs only when more heat is needed.
12. If you want to test control quickly, set a higher target for 1 hour. Watch to see if the room becomes warmer. Then return the hold to the default setting.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Target temperature | 5–30 °C in 0.5 °C steps | 20 °C |
| Hold duration | Until next schedule change, 1–12 hours, or permanent | Until next schedule change |

## Troubleshooting

- If the target temperature does not change, check that Child Lock is off. If the ring or screen is locked, go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > Lock**.
- If the temperature does not increase after you raise the target, wait a little longer. Boilers do not always heat a room at once.
- If the temperature is not easy to set, make sure you are moving in 0.5 °C steps. Go to **Menu > Heating > Manual** and try again slowly.
- If a manual change stops too soon, check the hold duration. Go to **Menu > Heating > Manual > Hold Duration**. The default is until the next schedule change.
- If the schedule changes after you want it to change, use the permanent hold for testing. Go to **Menu > Heating > Manual > Hold Duration** and choose **Permanent**. Remember to change it later.
- If the app cannot change the temperature, check that the app is signed in and the device is online. Check Wi-Fi if needed.
- If the wall unit is unresponsive, check the batteries or 24 V AC wiring. If the problem continues, contact support or your qualified installer.
- If the room temperature is not changing as expected, check that the wall unit is not in direct sunlight or above a radiator. This can affect the reading.

# Weekly Schedule

## How to

A weekly schedule sets temperatures for different times of the day and different days. This can help you heat the home when you are usually there and lower it when you are usually away.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule**. The schedule screen opens.
2. Choose the day you want to edit. You can edit each day of the week.
3. Set the number of periods for that day. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Periods Per Day**. You can set 1 to 6 periods per day. The default is 4 periods per day.
4. For each period, set a start time. Use the ring or touch screen to change the time. Use **Menu > Settings > Time Format** if the clock shows 12 h or 24 h in a way you do not want.
5. For each period, set a target temperature. Each period has a start time and a target temperature.
6. Repeat for each day. You can make weekdays different from weekends.
7. To save time, copy one day to other days. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Copy Day**. Choose the source day, then choose the other days you want to receive the same schedule.
8. If your schedule looks wrong, you can return to the default periods. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Default Periods**.
9. The default periods are 06:30 at 20 °C, 08:30 at 17 °C, 17:00 at 21 °C, and 22:30 at 16 °C. These are a starting point, not a requirement.
10. Check that each period makes sense. For example, one period may cover the morning. Another may cover the time when most people are out. Another may cover the evening.
11. Keep the schedule simple at first. Use four periods on weekdays and weekends. Change it later if needed.
12. Remember that manual holds, Away Mode, Boost, Holiday Mode, and Frost Protection can affect when the boiler runs. A schedule is your normal plan, but special modes can change heating temporarily.
13. In the app, open your home and go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule**. The same schedule settings can be checked and edited there.
14. After any schedule change, watch how the home heats for a day or two. Small changes are usually enough.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Periods per day | 1–6 | 4 |
| Copy day | Copy to any other days | — |
| Default periods | 06:30 20 °C; 08:30 17 °C; 17:00 21 °C; 22:30 16 °C | 06:30 20 °C; 08:30 17 °C; 17:00 21 °C; 22:30 16 °C |

## Troubleshooting

- If the schedule does not change the temperature, check that the schedule is active and your home is online. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule** and check the current period.
- If only four periods show, that is normal if you have not changed Periods Per Day. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Periods Per Day** and choose a value from 1 to 6.
- If one day has the wrong times, check Copy Day. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Copy Day** and copy the correct day to the affected days.
- If times look strange, check **Menu > Settings > Time Format**. Choose 12 h or 24 h.
- If the home is too cold in the morning, move an earlier period to a more comfortable temperature or slightly earlier time. Make small changes.
- If the home is too warm at night, lower the evening period temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule** and edit the evening period.
- If the schedule changes but the boiler does not run, the room may already be above the target temperature. Wait and check again.
- If the schedule returns to the default times, you may have used **Menu > Heating > Schedule > Default Periods**. Recreate your chosen periods.

# Away Mode and Geofencing

## How to

Away Mode lowers heating when everyone has left the home. Geofencing helps the thermostat know when household members have left the area. Geofencing is a virtual area on a map. When a phone leaves that area, the thermostat can treat the home as empty.

1. Open the Hearthline app and sign in. Make sure each household member has their own account where needed.
2. Turn on Away Mode in the app. The exact screen shows whether Away Mode is active.
3. Turn on geofencing for the household members you want to include. The thermostat will use phone location to help detect when everyone has left.
4. Set the geofence radius. Go to **Menu > Heating > Away > Geofence Radius**. You can set 200 m to 2,000 m. The default is 500 m.
5. A small radius, such as 200 m, can turn Away Mode on quickly. It may trigger if someone drives around a corner or walks a short distance away.
6. A large radius, such as 2,000 m, can be more reliable for large properties or rural areas. It may trigger less often on short trips.
7. Set Return pre-heat. Go to **Menu > Heating > Away > Return Pre-Heat**. This setting can turn on with the default option: on.
8. Return pre-heat starts heating before a phone comes back into the geofence area. It can help the home feel warmer when people arrive.
9. If you do not want heating to start before a return, set Return pre-heat to off. Then the home warms up after the return is detected.
10. Away Mode uses the eco temperature. When every household member’s phone has left the area, heating can drop to the eco temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature** to set that temperature.
11. Make sure all household members who should control Away Mode are in the household. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Users** and check the household list.
12. Remember that Away Mode should not turn on if one household member is still inside. The exact behavior depends on the phones detected in the area.
13. If you are testing Away Mode, leave the area with all household phones. Watch whether the thermostat uses the eco temperature.
14. If you use Guest users, remember that Guests cannot change the schedule. Check roles in **Menu > Multi-User > Roles** if someone cannot change settings they should not control.
15. If you go on holiday, use Holiday Mode instead of Away Mode. Holiday Mode has start and end dates. Away Mode is for normal daily absence.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Geofence radius | 200–2,000 m | 500 m |
| Return pre-heat | On or off | On |

## Troubleshooting

- If Away Mode does not turn on, check that every household member’s phone has left the geofence area. One phone in the area can keep the home in normal heating mode.
- If Away Mode turns on too often, increase the geofence radius. Go to **Menu > Heating > Away > Geofence Radius** and try a larger value such as 1,000 m or 2,000 m.
- If Away Mode turns on too late, reduce the geofence radius. Try 200 m to 500 m, but be aware it may trigger more often.
- If a phone does not seem to trigger Away Mode, check that the phone is associated with the household and that location services are allowed for the Hearthline app.
- If the home is cold when people return, check Return pre-heat. Go to **Menu > Heating > Away > Return Pre-Heat** and set it to on.
- If the home is warm before a return, set Return pre-heat to off. Go to **Menu > Heating > Away > Return Pre-Heat**.
- If Away Mode uses a temperature you do not expect, check the eco temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature** and review the value.
- If household users are missing, check the household list. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Users** and invite the correct accounts.

# Eco Temperature

## How to

Eco Temperature sets the lower temperature used when the thermostat is in an energy-saving state. Eco means economy. This temperature is commonly used by Away Mode when everyone has left the home.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature**. The current eco temperature appears.
2. Set the eco temperature. You can choose 10 °C to 20 °C. The default eco temperature is 16 °C.
3. Choose a lower eco temperature to save more energy. A lower value means less heat is used while the home is away.
4. Choose a higher eco temperature if you want the home to be warmer when you return. A higher value uses more energy.
5. Keep in mind that Frost Protection can still protect the home at the frost temperature. Frost Protection has its own setting and cannot be turned off.
6. If Away Mode is active, heating can use the eco temperature. The eco temperature is the target during away periods, unless another special mode is active.
7. If you often feel too cold when you return, raise the eco temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature** and increase it slightly. Try small steps.
8. If your energy use seems high when Away Mode is active, lower the eco temperature. But do not set it so low that the home is uncomfortable when you return.
9. If you are away for a planned period, check whether Holiday Mode is better. Holiday Mode uses holiday temperature and start or end dates.
10. If you use Boost, it can raise the temperature for a limited time. Eco Temperature remains your normal away target after Boost ends.
11. If you use Manual Control with a permanent hold, that manual temperature can override normal schedules. To test Eco Temperature, remove permanent manual holds first.
12. Review Eco Temperature each season. Homes may feel different in warm and cold weather.
13. Explain the eco temperature to other household members. This helps avoid accidental changes to the away setting.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Eco temperature | 10–20 °C | 16 °C |

## Troubleshooting

- If the home gets too cold when Away Mode is active, raise the eco temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Eco Temperature** and choose a higher value between 10 °C and 20 °C.
- If the home uses too much heat while away, lower the eco temperature. Try a value closer to the middle of the range first.
- If the eco temperature is grayed out or cannot be changed, check whether another mode is active. Check manual hold, Away Mode, Boost, or Holiday Mode.
- If the temperature does not drop when everyone leaves, Away Mode may not be active. Check the app and Away Mode status.
- If the temperature seems too high when you return, check Return pre-heat. Go to **Menu > Heating > Away > Return Pre-Heat**.
- If the home feels cold in cold weather, remember that the boiler needs time to warm walls and furniture. Give the home extra time after returning.
- If the eco temperature changes on its own, check whether another household user changed it. Review users in **Menu > Multi-User > Users**.

# Boost

## How to

Boost gives extra heat for a set time. It is useful when you want a short-term increase in temperature. Boost temperature is the target temperature plus 2 °C.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Boost**. The Boost screen opens.
2. Start Boost when you want extra heat. The screen shows that Boost is active.
3. During Boost, the target temperature becomes the default target plus 2 °C. If your normal target is 20 °C, Boost uses 22 °C while active.
4. Choose Boost duration. Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost > Boost Duration**. You can choose 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes.
5. The default Boost duration is 60 minutes. Use 30 minutes for a short warm-up. Use 120 minutes for a longer warm-up.
6. If you want to change the Boost temperature, go to **Menu > Heating > Boost > Boost Temperature**. The setting is the default target plus 2 °C.
7. If your target temperature changes, Boost still adds 2 °C to that normal target while it is active.
8. When Boost ends, heating returns to your normal setting or schedule. If there is no schedule, it returns to the last manual target that was active before Boost.
9. Do not use Boost as a permanent setting. It is meant for short-term extra heat.
10. If Boost does not seem to work, check whether Child Lock is on. Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > Lock** if needed.
11. If Boost stops early, check the duration. Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost > Boost Duration** and choose 60 minutes or more if needed.
12. If Boost does not make the home warmer, the room may be far below the target. A short boost may not be enough. Try a longer boost or use a higher normal target.
13. If Boost is used often, consider whether your normal target or schedule may be too low. Boost can help occasionally, but normal settings should match your comfort.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Boost duration | 30, 60, 90, or 120 minutes | 60 minutes |
| Boost temperature | Default target + 2 °C | Default target + 2 °C |

## Troubleshooting

- If Boost does not start, check that the wall unit is responsive and not locked. Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > Lock** to check the lock.
- If Boost ends too soon, check the duration. Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost > Boost Duration** and choose 90 or 120 minutes.
- If the home does not warm up enough during Boost, the boiler may need more time. Gas or oil boilers heat slowly. Try a longer Boost duration.
- If the Boost temperature is not the target plus 2 °C, check that Boost is still active. After it ends, the normal target returns.
- If Boost starts on its own, check scheduled settings or manual holds. Boost should be used as a short-term action.
- If the app and wall unit show different Boost states, refresh the app and check that the device is online.
- If the boiler runs for the full Boost time and still does not heat, check for boiler issues or ask a qualified installer to inspect the system.
- If Boost seems ineffective often, lower the duration to avoid unnecessary heat use. Go to **Menu > Heating > Boost > Boost Duration**.

# Hot Water Control

## How to

Hot Water Control is for homes with a hot-water cylinder. A cylinder is a hot-water storage tank. If your home does not have a cylinder, this chapter may not apply to your system.

1. Confirm that your home has a hot-water cylinder. The Hearthline T2 is used with gas or oil boilers that heat homes and can also heat hot water.
2. Check the current hot water state in the app or on the wall unit. The display helps you see whether hot water is being asked for.
3. Set a hot water schedule. Go to **Menu > Hot Water > Hot Water Schedule**.
4. Add periods for the day. You can use up to 3 periods per day. Use times when you most often use hot water.
5. For each period, choose the time range. Keep the schedule simple at first. A morning period and an evening period are a good start.
6. Save the hot water schedule. The thermostat will use these periods to ask for hot water when your normal schedule allows.
7. Use hot water boost when you need extra hot water sooner. Go to **Menu > Hot Water > Hot Water Boost**.
8. Set hot water boost duration. Choose 30 or 60 minutes. The default is 60 minutes.
9. Start the boost when you know you need extra hot water soon. Boost is for short-term extra demand.
10. After boost ends, normal hot water control returns. If a schedule is set, the next scheduled period applies.
11. If hot water does not heat as expected, check whether the schedule period is active and whether the home is online.
12. If a cylinder is slow to heat, boost may not make a full tank hot immediately. Give the system time to respond.
13. If multiple users control hot water, review roles. Guests cannot change the schedule. Check **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Hot water schedule | Up to 3 periods per day | — |
| Hot water boost | 30 or 60 minutes | 60 minutes |

## Troubleshooting

- If hot water is not available, check whether your home has a hot-water cylinder and that the boiler system is working normally.
- If hot water does not start at the expected time, check the hot water schedule. Go to **Menu > Hot Water > Hot Water Schedule**.
- If too many periods are confusing, reduce the number to one or two simple periods per day.
- If hot water boost is too short, go to **Menu > Hot Water > Hot Water Boost** and choose 60 minutes.
- If the hot water schedule seems to change on its own, check whether another household user changed it. Review users in **Menu > Multi-User > Users**.
- If the wall unit shows hot water control but hot water does not heat, wait a few minutes. Hot-water cylinders can take time to warm.
- If the app cannot control hot water, check that the device is online and that your user has the right to make changes.
- If you do not have a hot-water cylinder, hot water periods may not apply to your home. Check with your qualified installer.

# Holiday Mode

## How to

Holiday Mode keeps the home at a safe, lower temperature for a planned absence. It uses start and end dates and a holiday temperature.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday**. The holiday settings open.
2. Set the start date. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > Start Date**. Choose the day you plan to leave.
3. Set the end date. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > End Date**. Choose the day you expect to return.
4. Set the holiday temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > Holiday Temperature**. You can choose 5 °C to 15 °C. The default is 12 °C.
5. A lower holiday temperature saves more energy. A higher holiday temperature keeps the home warmer.
6. Start Holiday Mode before you leave. This gives the thermostat time to move to the holiday setting.
7. If you leave, the home can maintain the holiday temperature for the dates you chose. It does not follow normal comfort temperatures during those dates.
8. If you return early, end Holiday Mode before you get home. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday** and change the dates or turn off Holiday Mode if the app shows that option.
9. If you return late, extend the end date. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > End Date** and choose the new date.
10. If you go on holiday often, use Holiday Mode rather than Away Mode. Away Mode is for daily absence. Holiday Mode is for planned dates.
11. Remember that Frost Protection can still protect the home. Frost Protection cannot be turned off.
12. Before a long absence, check that the app shows the correct dates and holiday temperature. This avoids accidental heating or too much cooling.
13. After returning, check your normal schedule. Holiday Mode should not replace your weekly schedule.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Start and end dates | Dates | — |
| Holiday temperature | 5–15 °C | 12 °C |

## Troubleshooting

- If Holiday Mode does not start, check that the start date has arrived and is correct. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > Start Date**.
- If Holiday Mode ends too early, check the end date. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > End Date** and extend it if needed.
- If the home is too cold during a holiday, raise the holiday temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Holiday > Holiday Temperature**.
- If the home uses too much heat while away, lower the holiday temperature. Try small steps within 5 °C to 15 °C.
- If normal heating still runs during holiday dates, check whether Holiday Mode is active and whether the dates cover the current time.
- If another user changed the dates, check user roles. Guests cannot change the schedule. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.
- If the home feels very cold after a long holiday, allow extra time for it to warm up. Walls and floors may be cooler after days at a lower temperature.
- If the dates seem wrong in the app, refresh the app and check that the device is online.

# Frost Protection

## How to

Frost Protection turns heating on whenever the room falls below the frost temperature. This helps prevent too-cold conditions in the home. Frost Protection cannot be turned off.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Heating > Frost Protection**. The frost settings open.
2. Set the frost temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Frost Protection > Frost Temperature**. You can choose 5 °C to 12 °C. The default is 7 °C.
3. A lower frost temperature means heating turns on later. This can save heat but may allow the room to get cooler.
4. A higher frost temperature means heating turns on earlier. This keeps the home from getting too cold sooner.
5. If the room temperature falls below the frost temperature, heating can turn on even if normal heating is off. This protects the home from too-cold conditions.
6. If heating turns on at night or when away, check whether Frost Protection is active. This can happen when the room is below the frost temperature.
7. If the home is in a very cold location, choose a higher frost temperature within the available range. Try 10 °C or 12 °C if 7 °C feels too low.
8. If you want to save heat, choose a lower frost temperature within the available range. Try 5 °C or 6 °C, but make sure it suits your home.
9. Do not confuse Frost Protection with Holiday Mode. Holiday Mode uses holiday dates and a holiday temperature. Frost Protection works automatically.
10. If Frost Protection seems to run too often, the room may be below the frost temperature for long periods. This may mean the home needs insulation or a different normal target.
11. If the boiler runs often but the home stays cold, check the boiler system and ask a qualified installer if needed.
12. If you expect the home to be empty for a long time, use Holiday Mode with a suitable holiday temperature. Frost Protection still cannot be turned off.
13. Review the frost temperature once a year. Seasonal changes can change how quickly rooms cool.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Frost temperature | 5–12 °C | 7 °C |

## Troubleshooting

- If heating turns on when you expected it to stay off, check whether the room is below the frost temperature. Go to **Menu > Heating > Frost Protection > Frost Temperature**.
- If the home gets very cold, raise the frost temperature. Choose a value closer to 12 °C if needed.
- If the home uses too much heat in cold spells, lower the frost temperature carefully. Choose a value closer to 5 °C only if the home is comfortable and protected.
- If Frost Protection seems to run constantly, the room may be poorly insulated. Contact a qualified installer or heating specialist to check the system.
- If the frost temperature cannot be changed, check whether another mode is active. Review Away Mode, Holiday Mode, Boost, and manual holds.
- If the wall unit shows low battery, the reading or communication may be affected. Replace with two AA batteries if needed.
- If the boiler starts unexpectedly but the home stays cold, check for boiler faults. Ask a qualified installer to inspect the system.
- If you want a warmer empty home, use Holiday Mode rather than changing Frost Protection only.

# Energy Reports

## How to

Energy Reports help you understand how much your boiler runs. Boiler running hours mean the amount of time the boiler ran each day. The app shows a monthly summary. You can also receive a weekly email.

1. Open the Hearthline app and sign in to your home.
2. Go to the energy report screen. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Energy Reports**.
3. Check boiler running hours per day. The report shows how much the boiler ran for each day.
4. Use the report to compare similar days. For example, compare a weekend day with a weekday, or a warm week with a cold week.
5. Turn the weekly email on or off. Go to **Menu > Energy Reports > Weekly Email**. It is on by default.
6. If you want fewer emails, set Weekly Email to off. If you want a regular summary, leave it on.
7. Check the monthly summary in the app. The monthly summary is always on. You do not need to turn it on.
8. Use boiler running hours to spot changes. If the boiler runs much more than usual, your settings may have changed.
9. Compare running hours with temperature settings. A higher target temperature can cause longer boiler running hours.
10. Compare running hours with outside weather. Colder weather can increase boiler running hours.
11. Compare running hours before and after schedule changes. If a schedule change greatly increases hours, review the period times and temperatures.
12. If you changed Away Mode, Eco Temperature, or Holiday Mode, check how reports change afterward.
13. If you invite other users, remember that their changes can affect energy use. Review users in **Menu > Multi-User > Users**.
14. If the report is not useful yet, watch it for a full week. Energy patterns are easier to see over days, not minutes.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Weekly email | On or off | On |
| Monthly summary in the app | Always on | Always on |
| Boiler running hours shown per day | Shown per day | Shown per day |

## Troubleshooting

- If the weekly email does not arrive, check whether Weekly Email is on. Go to **Menu > Energy Reports > Weekly Email**.
- If the email is missing, check your email spam or junk folder. Email delivery can sometimes change without a thermostat setting changing.
- If the monthly summary seems wrong, check that the date range shown is correct in the app.
- If boiler running hours do not appear, check that the device is online and has recent data.
- If boiler running hours are very high, check your target temperatures and schedule. Go to **Menu > Heating > Schedule**.
- If boiler running hours are low but the home is cold, check the boiler system. Contact a qualified installer if needed.
- If users changed settings and you want to know who may have changed them, review users and roles in **Menu > Multi-User > Users** and **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.
- If reports are empty after installation, allow the device time to collect data from a boiler running period.

# Child Lock

## How to

Child Lock locks the ring and screen on the wall unit. This helps stop accidental changes by children. It does not stop the Hearthline app from being used by authorized users.

1. On the wall unit, go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock**.
2. Turn Lock on. Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > Lock** and choose on.
3. When you turn the lock on for the first time, set a PIN. Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > PIN**. A PIN is a 4-digit personal identification number.
4. Choose four digits. Do not use an obvious number such as 0000. Tell trusted adults the PIN, but do not share it widely.
5. Confirm the PIN. The wall unit should show that Child Lock is active.
6. When Child Lock is on, the ring and screen on the wall unit are locked. Children or guests may not change settings at the wall unit.
7. If a trusted adult needs to change settings, they can enter the PIN to use the wall unit if needed.
8. To turn Child Lock off, go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > Lock** and choose off.
9. To change the PIN, go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > PIN**. Set a new 4-digit PIN.
10. Keep the PIN safe. If it is forgotten, follow any recovery help shown in the app or contact support.
11. Child Lock does not remove Away Mode, Frost Protection, schedules, or app controls. It only protects the wall unit ring and screen.
12. If you have several trusted adults, make sure they know the PIN and how to lock or unlock the wall unit.
13. If you do not need the lock, keep it off. The default setting is off.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Lock | On or off | Off |
| PIN | 4 digits | Set when lock is first turned on |

## Troubleshooting

- If the ring does nothing, check whether Child Lock is on. Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > Lock**.
- If the screen does not respond to changes, check whether Child Lock is active. Unlock it with the 4-digit PIN if needed.
- If you forgot the PIN, keep the wall unit locked and check the app or support help for reset guidance.
- If the wall unit unlocks too easily, make sure the PIN is not obvious. Go to **Menu > Settings > Child Lock > PIN** and set a new 4-digit PIN.
- If children can still change settings in the app, check user roles. Guests cannot change the schedule. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.
- If the PIN is accepted but settings do not change, refresh the app and check that the device is online.
- If the lock seems to turn off by itself, check whether another user changed it. Review users in **Menu > Multi-User > Users**.
- If Child Lock does not stop all changes, remember that it locks the ring and screen on the wall unit, not the Hearthline app.

# Multi-User Access

## How to

Multi-User Access lets the owner invite household members. A home can have up to 8 users. Users can have different roles: Owner, Member, or Guest.

1. Open the Hearthline app and sign in as the account owner.
2. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Users**. The current household users are shown.
3. Invite a household member. Add their email or use the invitation option in the app.
4. The invited person accepts the invitation and signs in with their own Hearthline account.
5. Keep the number of users within the limit. A home can have up to 8 users.
6. Set the role for each person. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.
7. Choose Owner where needed. The Owner has the full account responsibility for the home.
8. Choose Member for household members who should use normal household controls.
9. Choose Guest for people who should have limited access. Guests cannot change the schedule.
10. Remember that Away Mode and Multi-User Access work together. The geofence can depend on household members’ phones.
11. If a household member moves out, remove or change their role when appropriate. Keep the household list accurate.
12. If someone cannot change a schedule, check their role. Guests cannot change the schedule. Members and Owners can use normal household controls.
13. If a new person should help manage settings, check whether a Member role is enough before adding more full accounts.
14. If you have a child or guest who should not control heating, use a limited role where appropriate.
15. If you use Child Lock, remember that it protects the wall unit. User roles protect what can be changed in the app.

## Settings

| Setting | Options or range | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Users | Up to 8 per home | — |
| Roles | Owner, Member, Guest; Guests cannot change the schedule | — |

## Troubleshooting

- If an invitation does not appear, check that the invited person uses the correct email and has the Hearthline app installed.
- If you cannot add another user, check the home limit. A home can have up to 8 users.
- If someone is still listed after leaving the household, remove or change their role from **Menu > Multi-User > Users**.
- If a user cannot change the schedule, check their role. Guests cannot change the schedule. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.
- If a user cannot be removed, check whether the person is signed in and whether the account owner has permission to edit users.
- If Away Mode does not consider a phone, check whether that user is part of the household list. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Users**.
- If a Guest seems able to change schedule-like settings, check whether the account is actually listed as Guest. Go to **Menu > Multi-User > Roles**.
- If the household list looks wrong, refresh the app and check that the device is online.

# Error Codes

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | No Wi-Fi connection | Check that the device is near your 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network. Check the Wi-Fi password and router status. Reconnect in **Menu > Getting Started > Wi-Fi**. |
| E2 | Temperature sensor fault | Do not open the wall unit or receiver box yourself. Contact a qualified installer or support. |
| E3 | Receiver not responding | Keep the wall unit within 30 m indoors of the receiver box. Check that the receiver has mains power. Contact a qualified installer if it still does not respond. |
| E4 | Wall unit battery low | Replace with two AA batteries. If the wall unit uses 24 V AC wiring, ask a qualified installer to check the power wiring. |
| E5 | Firmware update failed | Check that the device is online, then try again. If it fails again, contact support or your qualified installer. |

# Specifications

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Product | Hearthline T2 smart thermostat for homes with a gas or oil boiler |
| Wall unit | Wall unit with a 3.5-inch touch screen and a rotating ring |
| Receiver box | Receiver box wired next to the boiler |
| App | Hearthline app for iOS and Android |
| Wall unit power | Runs on 2 AA batteries, with about 2 years of battery life, or 24 V AC wiring |
| Receiver power | Receiver box is mains powered |
| Wi-Fi | Wi-Fi: 2.4 GHz only |
| Radio range | The receiver and wall unit talk to each other by radio at up to 30 m indoors |
| Installation | Installation of the receiver box must be done by a qualified installer; the manual covers setup after that |
